problem: A screen survives rotation but loses its in-memory state after process death.
reading: The lifecycle boxes are states of one screen, not four Activity objects. Compare the changing Activity identity with the retained ViewModel and the separately restored saved bundle.

problem: Unfolding a message screen must not discard its selection or scroll position.
reading: One hoisted selection feeds both presentations. A list selection updates that owner; width policy changes visible panes rather than inventing a second selection.

problem: The main thread is waiting on a lock while its holder performs disk work.
reading: Follow the labelled wait to the holder. The reason and repair boxes are diagnostic context, not extra threads or a runtime message pipeline.

problem: An obfuscated crash cannot be diagnosed with a mapping from a different build.
reading: The release identity selects the matching mapping. Obfuscated frames and that mapping are both inputs to retracing; a readable trace still needs reproduction.

problem: Two runs of the same APK can differ because ART has learned different hot paths.
reading: Execution records selected hot code in a profile. Background compilation can consume that profile; a later run can use compiled code. This is not app-triggered compilation.

problem: A profile file existing in the build does not prove that a user journey became faster.
reading: Read this as a generation-and-verification workflow. Device compilation state is checked before comparing the same journey; arrows are dependencies, not an install trace.

problem: A reminder or sync works with the screen on but is deferred while the device is idle.
reading: Device power state gates ordinary jobs, standard alarms and network access. Read each restricted resource against the same Doze state; these resources do not pass work to one another.

problem: Repeated retries after login may consume power without delivering useful work.
reading: This is an experiment workflow. Observed activity supports a hypothesis; only a controlled repeat can test the policy change. It is not a per-app energy attribution trace.

problem: A slow image analyzer must not work through every stale camera frame.
reading: One ImageProxy is being analyzed. With KEEP_ONLY_LATEST, newer pending frames replace stale ones; closing the current proxy permits delivery of the latest image.

problem: A ViewModel cannot request an Activity-scoped toolbar controller from a sibling component.
reading: Arrows show Hilt component parentage. Bindings are visible through ancestors, not sibling branches. Follow Fragment upward for ImageLoader; ViewModel has no path through ActivityComponent.

problem: Pointer input can open a row while accessibility users cannot activate it.
reading: Compare two independent semantics trees. Arrows denote focus or action progression within each tree, not data moving from the broken row into the fixed one.

problem: Back should remove Profile, and logout should leave no authenticated destination reachable.
reading: The app owns a list of destination keys. Home and Profile illustrate push/pop; Login is the replacement signed-out root, not another entry that must remain underneath.

groups.label: Destination keys used in this example

problem: A stuttering feed may be decoding images on Main rather than recomposing too often.
reading: This is a diagnostic workflow: establish a repeatable journey, measure a representative build, locate the expensive phase, then verify one focused repair.

problem: Another app cannot read an invoice by using its private filesystem path.
reading: A FileProvider URI names the shareable file; a temporary grant authorizes the recipient. The recipient reads through ContentResolver, without gaining access to every private file.

edges.label: map configured file to content URI

problem: Copied Gradle settings drift when fifty modules each maintain their own policy.
reading: The module resolves a convention plugin from the included build. That plugin composes base and optional capabilities; consumer builds verify the resulting shared policy.

problem: A low fleet-wide crash rate can hide a severe failure loop in one release cohort.
reading: Capture, reporting, impact assessment and response have different responsibilities. Arrows describe the investigation workflow; captured events are not guaranteed to reach a dashboard.

edges.label: report when capture and delivery succeed

problem: An overlapping avatar row must respect constraints and mirror correctly in RTL.
reading: The layout measures each child once, selects its own constrained size, then places the same child identities with logical start-relative coordinates.

groups.label: Children measured and placed by this layout

problem: Two simultaneous settings edits must not overwrite each other with stale snapshots.
reading: Both callers submit transforms to one DataStore instance. Updates are serialized and durably persisted; data Flow exposes committed state, rather than a separate application cache.

problem: Rotation recreates Activity-scoped bindings but must preserve retained and ViewModel-scoped bindings.
reading: Arrows are component parentage, not callback order. Compare component lifetime labels as the same screen rotates, finishes and finally loses its process.

problem: Finding a BLE device does not mean its measurement stream is ready.
reading: User intent governs the session. Scanning, connection and service setup precede a configured subscription; only that ready subscription can deliver measurement values.

problem: A disconnected BLE handle must not become an unbounded reconnect loop.
reading: The product intent outlives one connection. A disconnect leads to a policy check; a bounded retry creates a fresh connection only while the feature is still wanted.

problem: A Fragment can survive on the back stack after its old view is destroyed.
reading: Observer lifetime follows its LifecycleOwner. The Fragment-owned registration survives view destruction; a view-owned registration is removed with that view. Callback text is a trace, not another owner.

edges.label: creates a new view after return

problem: Renaming a user in one operation should update another watcher of the same cached entity.
reading: The mutation and watcher meet at one normalized record identity. Notification depends on matching cache IDs and selected fields; unrelated or missing data needs an explicit policy.

problem: Saving Health Connect progress before applying its changes can silently skip records after a crash.
reading: The token selects a changes page. This illustrative app transaction commits data and matching progress together; Health Connect does not transact the app-owned database for you.

problem: A missing dependency is detected at different points by different wiring configurations.
reading: Compare independent approaches to the same missing binding. No arrow joins them: manual construction, Hilt validation and an unchecked Koin DSL graph are alternatives, not pipeline stages.

problem: Shortening drawing code cannot fix a frame whose Main thread is waiting for a lock.
reading: The wait edge identifies the dependency in this example. Frame selection and retesting are investigation steps; fewer recompositions alone do not demonstrate smoother frames.

groups.label: Threads involved in the blocking example

problem: Recompiled source can pass while an already compiled caller still requests a removed method descriptor.
reading: Old binaries and recompiled source are separate compatibility tests against the candidate. The gate combines their evidence; a default argument does not rewrite an existing caller binary.

problem: A shared service must not outlive the platform resources injected into it.
reading: This illustrative composition root constructs target resources and injects them. The declared graph lifetime determines when those resources are closed; rendering a screen is not automatic teardown.

problem: Adding a web target can expose a dependency that never published a compatible implementation.
reading: The new target imposes support requirements on the dependency seam. Existing success is separate evidence; the product must choose a supported replacement, adapter or narrower scope.

problem: One shared request API still executes through different platform networking engines.
reading: Follow request preparation into the selected engine, then map its response or failure back to the domain boundary. Cancellation and transport behavior require evidence for that engine.

problem: A widget must reject an incomplete or unsupported snapshot rather than display invented consistency.
reading: This is an explicit single-writer design, not a guarantee provided by shared Kotlin. The reader validates a complete versioned value and applies its fallback when that value is unusable.

problem: A new application must open databases from every still-supported old schema version.
reading: The stored version selects the required upgrade path. Migration code transforms existing data, while upgrade tests check preservation; a successful fresh install is a different case.

problem: A shared weather feature needs location without importing an Android Context or Apple controller.
reading: Shared code depends on a platform-neutral contract. The supplied adapter implements that contract; the explicit owner governs construction, cancellation and resource cleanup in this example.

problem: Common Kotlin source does not become one universal Android-and-Apple binary.
reading: The same common sources participate in separate target compilations. Each target supplies applicable platform code and produces its own output; Consumer represents the corresponding app role.

problem: Uploading symbols does not prove that a real crash report can identify a shared-code failure.
reading: The controlled event, release identity and matching platform symbols converge at the report. Android mappings and Apple dSYMs remain distinct artifacts, matched to their actual distributed build.

problem: A shared-code migration needs a reversible pilot rather than an all-at-once rewrite.
reading: Both implementations are alternatives behind one product contract. Baseline and pilot evidence inform expansion or rollback; no arrow means copying live state between competing implementations.

problem: A green JVM job cannot establish that a changed Apple consumer still links and behaves correctly.
reading: Required target checks feed the release decision independently. Select jobs from affected promises; Apple-capable integration evidence is separate from common-code or JVM success.

problem: A dismissed Swift screen can remain retained by its shared observer callback.
reading: Arrows are strong references in this illustrative cross-runtime cycle. Ending presentation does not break them; removing the registered callback removes the unwanted ownership path.

problem: A repository fallback test must control transport failure and cached data without claiming real-platform coverage.
reading: The repository calls controlled collaborators and exposes an observable outcome. Assertions cover the declared fallback and request parameters; real engines and exported Apple APIs require separate tests.

problem: Durable sync intent must survive periods when the platform grants no execution opportunity.
reading: The outbox and stored outcome are durable application state. A platform opportunity permits only bounded work; unfinished operations remain for a later allowed opportunity.

problem: A platform transport exception should become a domain outcome that an iOS screen can handle.
reading: Follow the safe mapping path from platform failure to Offline UI. The unsafe exception-escape case in the steps specifically concerns the Objective-C export path; other export bridges have their own contracts.

problem: Declaring a dependency in commonMain cannot manufacture an unsupported target artifact.
reading: Selection combines the requested library, concrete consumer attributes and producer variants. These are converging inputs, not four sequential compilation phases.

problem: A Swift package checksum must describe the exact XCFramework archive that consumers download.
reading: A tested release build produces an archive. Reviewed metadata binds its version, URL and checksum; an independent app resolves and exercises that exact artifact.

edges.label: bind exact archive URL and checksum

problem: Cancelling a Swift Task does not by syntax alone prove that its Kotlin operation stopped.
reading: The selected bridge is the cancellation boundary to test. The arrows show the requested propagation path; terminal state and callback cleanup must be observed for that bridge and version.

problem: A shared checkout surface and its native host must not each navigate independently after completion.
reading: This illustrative design keeps top-level navigation in the native coordinator. Shared UI owns internal checkout steps and reports one semantic event to that owner.

problem: A generated resource accessor compiling does not prove that translated text ships and renders correctly.
reading: Follow reviewed catalog input through generation and publication into a real consumer. Final-app checks cover locale, placeholders and layout rather than only the library compilation.

problem: A rejected debug log can still pay for an expensive eagerly evaluated argument.
reading: The call evaluates its ordinary argument before entering the runtime filter. Only accepted output reaches the sink; a rejected message does not undo the earlier calculation.

problem: A faster benchmark number may reflect different device or compilation conditions rather than a real fix.
reading: Controls make measurements comparable. A corresponding trace supports one hypothesis, which must be challenged by another controlled run. This is an evidence loop, not an application data pipeline.

problem: A long-lived callback registry can keep an obsolete screen strongly reachable.
reading: The two reference arrows show why the old screen remains alive. Heap evidence identifies that retaining path; it is not another object that owns the screen.

problem: A network request finishing is not the same boundary as Checkout becoming useful on screen.
reading: Instrumented requests can carry trace context to participating servers. The user interaction ends at its defined ready-UI condition; missing spans and sampling limit correlation evidence.
